- When sentiment turns negative or shows strong downward momentum (e.g., sentiment change > -0.67 or sudden drops), model tends to overcorrect or overshoot downward — reduce forecast lag or dampen early decline.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >75.0), model often overreacts with exaggerated continuation — cap forecast peak or apply mean reversion after 3–5 days.
- If sentiment is neutral or weak (e.g., sentiment level < 0.5 or change < 0.33), model frequently overestimates upside — adjust upward bias downward by 0.5–1.0 units.
- When news volume drops to 0, model often fails to adjust — force a 1–2 day lag correction or reduce forecast volatility.
- Model consistently overestimates short-term (1–3 day) reversals — apply smoothing filter or reduce sensitivity to recent sentiment swings.
- If sentiment shows strong upward momentum (e.g., sentiment > 0.67 and rising), model often fails to peak early — delay forecast peak by 1–2 days or reduce overshoot.
- Mean reversion is underutilized — if price deviates >2σ from 30-day moving average, apply correction toward mean with 50% weight on sentiment direction.
